title: ndgrid
summary: Generate full coordinate arrays for an N-D rectangular grid.

gpu_support.notes: RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs, materializes dense grids on the host, and uploads outputs when GPU residency is requested. Providers may supply a future ndgrid hook to avoid the round trip.

description: `ndgrid` expands one or more coordinate vectors into dense N-D coordinate arrays. Each output `Xi` contains copies of the ith grid vector along dimension `i`.
behaviors: `X = ndgrid(x)` returns `x` as a column-vector grid.
`[X1, X2, ..., Xn] = ndgrid(xg)` reuses the single vector `xg` for every requested output dimension.
`[X1, X2, ..., Xn] = ndgrid(x1, x2, ..., xn)` returns one grid per input vector.
Input vectors may be row vectors, column vectors, scalars, or higher-rank arrays with at most one non-singleton dimension.
The output size is `[length(x1), length(x2), ..., length(xn)]`; the one-output form uses `length(x) x 1`.

Each output preserves the corresponding input axis class independently: complex axes produce complex outputs, logical axes produce logical outputs, and dense numeric tensors preserve their RunMat dtype metadata.
Requesting more outputs than supplied vectors is an error unless the single-vector syntax is used.

faqs.question: How is `ndgrid` different from `meshgrid`?
faqs.answer: `ndgrid` uses the first input along the first dimension, the second input along the second dimension, and so on. `meshgrid` swaps the first two dimensions for plotting-oriented X/Y grids.

faqs.question: How many dimensions can `ndgrid` create?
faqs.answer: As many as the requested output count in the single-vector syntax, or as many as the number of supplied vectors in the multi-vector syntax.

faqs.question: What happens with empty vectors?
faqs.answer: Empty vectors produce empty dense grids with the corresponding zero extent.

faqs.question: Can `ndgrid` return gpuArray outputs?
faqs.answer: Yes. gpuArray inputs request gpuArray outputs; RunMat currently gathers inputs, materializes dense grids on the host, and uploads outputs through the owning provider. Upload failures raise an error instead of silently returning host arrays.

points: `[X1, X2, ..., Xn] = ndgrid(xg)` reuses a single grid vector for every requested dimension.
`X = ndgrid(x)` returns a one-dimensional grid as a column vector.
